The sequence starts with 1000 and \( x \), and each subsequent term is obtained by subtracting the preceding term from the one before that. We need to find the positive integer \( x \) that maximizes the length of the sequence before encountering the first negative term.

The sequence follows the pattern:
\[
\begin{align*}
\text{term}_1 &= 1000, \\
\text{term}_2 &= x, \\
\text{term}_3 &= 1000 - x, \\
\text{term}_4 &= x - (1000 - x) = 2x - 1000, \\
\text{term}_5 &= (1000 - x) - (2x - 1000) = 2000 - 3x, \\
\text{term}_6 &= (2x - 1000) - (2000 - 3x) = 5x - 3000, \\
\text{term}_7 &= (2000 - 3x) - (5x - 3000) = 5000 - 8x, \\
&\vdots
\end{align*}
\]

The coefficients of \( x \) and the constants follow the Fibonacci sequence with alternating signs. The key is to find \( x \) such that the terms stay positive as long as possible. 

Through analysis, it was found that the optimal \( x \) is approximately \( \frac{1000}{\text{golden ratio}} \approx 618 \). Testing \( x = 618 \) results in the sequence:
\[
1000, 618, 382, 236, 146, 90, 56, 34, 22, 12, 10, 2, 8, -6
\]
which has 14 terms before encountering the first negative term. Testing other values near 618 showed shorter sequences.

Thus, the positive integer \( x \) that produces a sequence of maximum length is \(\boxed{618}\).
